Kavarskas New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Utena County, Lithuania

Not demolished. This is the newer of Kavarskas's two Jewish cemeteries, a companion to the Old cemetery documented elsewhere in this collection. Jews began settling in Kavarskas in the 18th century, reaching 979 people (63 percent) by 1897, and supported a Jewish congregation with its own rabbi by the late 19th century. Expelled by the retreating Russian army in 1915, only about half the community returned after WWI; by 1923, 436 Jews remained, supported by a Jewish primary school and library. Zionist organizations remained active until the 1940 Soviet occupation. When the Germans invaded in 1941, Lithuanian nationalists murdered 30 Jewish men and women even before German troops reached the town; the rest were transferred to Ukmergė and shot on September 5, 1941.
